30.0.0.en: 1- "I will extol thee, O Lord: for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me."

30.0.1.en: 1- This psalm begins with thanksgiving to God, indeed with glorifying and magnifying Him, because there is no god like Him in His care and providence for His children; therefore David thanks Him for His works with him.

30.0.2.en: 2- David was sunk in his sin and did not feel its guilt, so God intervened by means of Nathan the prophet and warned him, and he awoke and rose to thank God, who drew him out of the mire of sin in which he had been immersed, and lifted him to the glory of purity and cleanness that he obtained by God's forgiveness.

30.0.3.en: 3- The nations around David, and likewise the demons, wanted to destroy David, but they were not able, because God delivered him and drew him out of their hands, so they could not rejoice over him.

30.0.4.en: 4- David feels God's special care for him, so he says, "thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me"; he feels that he is the object of God's care, love and protection from his enemies.

30.0.5.en: 5- The same words apply to King Hezekiah, who was exposed to destruction at the hand of Sennacherib the Assyrian, and likewise to sickness, and God rescued him and killed the army of Sennacherib, and healed him of his sickness.

30.0.6.en: 6- This verse applies to every spiritual person who strives with God against the demons and sin, and feels the hand of God that supports him and rescues him in the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, and so he glorifies Him.

30.1.0.en: 2- "O Lord my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me."

30.1.1.en: 1- God is able to do all things and loves His children, but He waits for their faith in Him, which appears in their taking refuge in Him and crying out to Him, and then He intervenes with power and delivers them from all evil.

30.1.2.en: 2- David has the boldness of sonship before God, so he says to Him "my God," and cries out to Him, and God rejoices in David's clinging to Him and answers his request.

30.1.3.en: 3- God heals His children, not only of the diseases of the body, but also of spiritual diseases, which are sins. And His healing is complete, as David rose up with all his strength and continued his life with God in prayers and good works.

30.2.0.en: 3- "O Lord, thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, from among those that go down to the pit."

30.2.1.en: 1- David was exposed to death from his Jewish enemies close to him, such as Saul and Absalom, and he was also exposed to death from the nations around him, such as the Philistines, and likewise he was exposed to spiritual death through his falling into sin. But God brought him up from death and the grave and gave him life before Him; therefore he thanks Him.

30.2.2.en: 2- What is meant by the pit here is death and the grave, and the hardest thing about the pit is that it is a deep hole that separates one from life and from people. It signifies man's separation from God by his fall and his going down to hell. So he thanks God who saved him from this death.

30.2.3.en: 3- King Hezekiah was exposed to death twice: at the hand of Sennacherib, then by sickness, but God gave him a new life. So David, by the spirit of prophecy, speaks of Hezekiah, who received the grace of life from death (Isa 36-39).

30.2.4.en: 4- David was a type of Christ who died and was buried in the tomb, then rose from it by the resurrection, to be the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, and to give those who believe in Him a rising from sin and every weakness.

30.2.5.en: The power of God is able to rescue you from any tribulation or sin, so do not be troubled by the difficulty of the tribulation, nor by your weakness, but rise quickly in repentance and prayer, and be confident that God will support you, and you will glorify Him.

30.3.0.en: 4- "Sing unto the Lord, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness."

30.3.1.en: 1- The pious are those who fear God and feel their unworthiness of His mercies and blessings, so when God blesses them they sing in thanksgiving and joy, and they sing with all their hearts. Only the pious are those to whom God gives joy and praise, but those who do not fear God easily fall into murmuring and cannot praise Him.

30.3.2.en: 2- The pious who fear God live in righteousness, because they are influenced by the holiness and righteousness of God, and they are always occupied with the beauty of God, so they praise Him and always remember His holiness. And the more they bless God and remember His holiness, the more their hearts are drawn to holiness and righteousness in all their conduct.

30.3.3.en: 3- Remembering the name of God and His holiness is the foundation of the dedication and blessing of any house. And this is the first reference to dedication in this psalm. And you also: the blessing of your life comes by remembering the holiness of God every day.

30.3.4.en: 4- David, who experienced the life of praise and enjoyed it, was moved in his heart toward the rest of the believers, so he calls them to share with him in praise and in remembering the holiness of God; for he is a member of the people of God and cannot be separated from them, just as the Christian is a member of the Church and does not feel life apart from his brethren.

30.4.0.en: 5- "For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: at evening weeping lodgeth, and in the morning singing."

30.4.1.en: 1- The tenderness of God, who desires that all be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth, appears in that He is angry with His children for a very short time, expressed here as a moment, so that they feel the guilt of sin, and He disciplines them, and they turn away from it and reject it; then God's mercies and favor come in a complete, happy life that the believers in Him live. So God was angry with David when he numbered the people, and struck them with the plague, but He quickly returned and forgave them, and David offered a sacrifice in the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite (2 Sam 24:25).

30.4.2.en: 2- Life is in God's favor, but distance from Him is death; therefore the children of God seek to please Him by keeping His commandments, and when they please Him they receive His abundant blessings, so they thank Him and rejoice.

30.4.3.en: 3- David speaks to us of weeping in the evening, that is, by a person's examining himself for his sins throughout the day, so that he regrets them and confesses them before God in tears, then sleeps quietly, and wakes to praise God who kept him through the night and granted him to begin a new day.

30.4.4.en: 4- Christ died on the cross and was buried in the evening, and the Marys and all His beloved wept for Him, but on the morning of the Resurrection His beloved saw the tomb empty, and He even appeared to them, and they rejoiced in His resurrection.

30.4.5.en: 5- The evening signifies our life in the world, where we suffer many pains and tribulations, expressed here as weeping, but in the morning of eternity, that is, when we enter the Kingdom of Heaven, we live in singing and praise forever.

30.4.6.en: 6- In the evening Sennacherib the Assyrian reproached the people of God, and they were in grief and weeping, and in the morning the Jews were rid of the Assyrians, for they found them corpses after the angel had killed them, while the rest fled. And in the evening King Hezekiah grieved over his sickness that would lead to his death, and in the morning God gave him a new lifespan of fifteen years (Isa 36-39).

30.4.7.en: Do not forget to examine yourself every night, and as much as you regret your sins God gives you hope and forgives you your sins, and after this you begin with great spiritual vigor.

30.5.s.en: (3) Asking the Savior and praising Him

30.5.0.en: 6- "And in my prosperity I said, I shall never be moved."

30.5.1.en: 1- David expresses his security in his earlier life, when he was tending the sheep, and felt the hand of God with him, and killed the lion and the bear. And when he saw Goliath he was not troubled but remained secure, and went out to him and killed him.

30.5.2.en: 2- Adam also lived securely in Paradise with God, enjoying fellowship with Him, and was far from sin, so he felt that he would live in this security forever.

30.5.3.en: 3- King Hezekiah felt security when God healed him of his sickness and prolonged his life, but in pride he opened his treasuries to show his greatness to the Babylonians who had come to congratulate him on his recovery, so he lost his peace, and God was angry with him, and his children were taken captive years after his death (2 Kgs 20:13).

30.5.4.en: 4- Perhaps David, in his negligence when he went up to the roof of his house, felt a false security, and fell into adultery with the wife of Uriah the Hittite (2 Sam 11:1-5). And perhaps he also became proud when he numbered the people, and God's punishment came upon him in the plague.

30.6.0.en: 7- "Lord, by thy favour thou hast made my mountain to stand strong: thou didst hide thy face, and I was troubled."

30.6.1.en: 1- David declares that the cause of his strength and might is God's favor toward him. And if the mountain signifies strength and steadfastness, David declares that his mountain, that is, his life, became steadfast and strong by God's favor toward him. In this he attributes the stability of his kingdom and his many victories to God's favor toward him. So David declares here his return to God and his reliance on Him, and not on his personal strength, because of which he fell into the sins of pride, adultery and the numbering of the people.

30.6.2.en: 2- At the same time David makes clear his concern for God's favor toward him, for as much as he keeps His commandments and submits to Him, he is established in his spiritual life and in his kingdom and his leadership of the people and his victories over the nations.

30.6.3.en: 3- The steadfastness of the mountain also applies to the kingdom of the children of Israel and its capital Jerusalem, which was built upon five mountains; if Jerusalem pleased God, He established it so that it became great and the nations were subject to it. But if it disobeyed His commandments it was disciplined by captivity and made subject to the nations, then if it returned to Him in repentance He brought it back from captivity and established it again.

30.6.4.en: 4- David declares that he needs God's constant care, for if God forsakes him and hides His face he is in fear and terror, and his enemies overcome him; so he declares his constant need of God's care, which is the cause of his strength. And so all the children of God and His Church declare their constant need of His care, that they may live before Him. For this reason also Moses refused that God should abandon His people when they fell into the worship of the golden calf, and because of Moses' clinging to God, God forgave His people and led them in the wilderness (Ex 33:15-17).

30.7.0.en: 8- "I cried to thee, O Lord; and unto the Lord I made supplication."

30.7.1.en: 1- Since David believed that his life is in God's favor, and that if He turns His face away from him he is afraid and terrified, he cried out to God, because He is his only help, and in Him he finds his life.

30.7.2.en: 2- Crying out is not by raising the voice, but by the entreaty of the heart, tears, and clinging to God; therefore God hears and cares and watches over, and indeed also lifts up His children.

30.7.3.en: 3- Supplication to the Lord shows David's humility and persistence, for he feels that he is a servant begging his master, and he makes supplication to Him from the depth of his heart that He may rescue him. And God looks upon the prayer of the poor and the humble, and hastens to him.

30.8.0.en: 9- "What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise thee? shall it declare thy truth?"

30.8.1.en: 1- David reproaches God with the boldness of sonship and says to Him, why do You leave me and not hear my cry? For without You I shall perish, and my life will end by my being put in the pit, or the dust, that is, the grave, and I shall lose my sonship to You and my enjoyment of fellowship with You forever in the Kingdom. In this he urges God to hasten to him to rescue him from every sin, and to support him in his life on earth.

30.8.2.en: 2- David also reproaches God and asks Him to hasten to his aid, because he wants to praise God, and to go on praising Him forever in the Kingdom. But if he dies while far from God, he will lose the ability to praise God, and praising God is the hope of his life.

30.8.3.en: 3- Those who do not pray and do not praise God are dead in the sight of God, although outwardly they are alive and move about on the earth, but the mark of the living is prayer and praise. And in proportion to one's concern for prayer, a person is alive.

30.8.4.en: 4- The spiritual person always thanks God, and declares God's faithfulness and truth, because he loves God. And when he declares God's faithfulness and praises Him, he thereby calls others to love the faithful God in His care and love for His children.

30.8.5.en: 5- Christ says to all the sinners who refused to believe in Him, what profit is there in my death on the cross and my going down to the tomb, that is, the pit? For you have not benefited from my death for you, and you, O sinners, have become dead, that is, dust, who do not pray, nor praise, nor declare my truth.

30.9.0.en: 10- "Hear, O Lord, and have mercy upon me: Lord, be thou my helper."

30.9.1.en: 1- David continued in his prayers before God, because he feels that He is his only refuge. So he repeats here his request to God to hear his prayer, and in this David is reassured, and even waits for God to answer him and make him feel His care, so that his heart rejoices.

30.9.2.en: 2- David's asking for mercy shows his humility and his confession of his sins before God, and that he needs God's mercy in order to live. And in proportion to David's repentance and humility he receives abundant mercies, however great his sins. And so David sees Christ not as a judge, but as an intercessor and forgiver of sins.

30.9.3.en: 3- Despite David's many experiences, he is confident that he has no success except with God's support and help, so he asks God to enter into every detail of his life, and in this he enjoys fellowship with Him, and secures the safety of his way and his success in all his steps, and this moves him to constant thanksgiving to God, so he enjoys true joy.

30.10.0.en: 11- "Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness;"

30.10.1.en: 12- "To the end that my soul may sing praise to thee, and not be silent. O Lord my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever." Girded me: clothed me with a girdle, and the girdle is what is worn around the waist and extends to the upper thighs.

30.10.2.en: 1- By David's offering repentance and asking God's mercies, he received His forgiveness, and God wiped away his tears, so his weeping turned into joy and spiritual dancing, that is, gladness of heart. For in repentance sorrow and joy mingle together at one and the same time in a wonderful way, so that joy covers the tears, and the feelings of regret melt away in the hands of the tender, forgiving God.

30.10.3.en: 2- David in his abasement before God had put on sackcloth, which is coarse clothing that declares his weakness and his austerity from the world, and his seeking God. And when he continued in fasting and prayers, God stretched out His hand and took off from him the garments of abasement, and clothed him with garments of joy. And He strengthened him with joy, because one who is girded about the waist shows strength and readiness to set out, for his heart was filled with joy, and he became ready for every good work and every self-giving service; that is, filled with hope and readiness to make others happy.

30.10.4.en: 3- Before the great works of God that David saw in himself, his spirit expressed its joy in singing and praise, after its silence for a long time because of its grief over its sins. And so life returned to his spirit, because prayer and praise are the delight of life.

30.10.5.en: 4- At the end David's boldness before God appears, for he feels his sonship to God and calls Him "my God," for he feels that God is his Lord and his God and the One responsible for him, so he praises Him for His works, not only in this life, but forever. And this shows David's faith in the other life after death, and his confidence in the love of God, who grants him the glories of the Kingdom.

30.10.6.en: 5- David's giving thanks to God forever indicates his joy in God his Savior, and his thanks to Him for all that he passes through in his life, and that this joy lasts forever.

30.10.7.en: Be diligent in prayer at all times, so that you see God as the tender Father who forgives your sins, and so you are encouraged however much you fall, and rejoice in God's love and thank Him continually.

30.10.8.en: My hope in God my Savior. To the chief Musician. A Psalm of David: "In thee, O Lord, do I put my trust" (v. 1). Introduction:

30.10.10.en: 2- It is among the psalms of thanksgiving, which are (Pss 30-34).

30.10.12.en: a - When he was fleeing from the face of Saul, and probably he was in the region of Maon.

30.10.13.en: b - Another opinion is that he was fleeing from Absalom his son.

30.10.14.en: c - Perhaps when David sinned his sin with the wife of Uriah the Hittite, then returned to God in repentance and trusted in Him, he wrote this psalm.

30.10.15.en: 4- This psalm calls to trust in God and to entrust one's life to Him, then to thank Him for His works; this psalm strengthens the faith of everyone who meets with troubles.

30.10.16.en: 5- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
